title: A fixed positive Cartan metric and a timelike compensator retain only spatial SO(3)

claim.statement: In the SO(2,3) fundamental, a positive Cartan metric has SO(2)xSO(3) stabilizer, a timelike compensator has SO(1,3) stabilizer, and their joint stabilizer is only SO(3).
claim.implication: The positive metric that stabilizes compact-first alignment cannot remain as a fixed physical background in a Lorentz-invariant low-energy gravity phase.

interpretation: The Cartan metric selects the full two-time plane; the compensator selects one axis in that plane.
Together they leave only rotations of the three spacelike axes and hence define a preferred rest frame.
Compact-first vacuum selection can remain useful only if the positive structure is auxiliary, transforms as a spurion and is removed, or decouples from observables after continuation.
falsifiers: An alternative positive structure whose joint stabilizer with the compensator is SO(1,3) would evade the result; no positive definite metric can be invariant under noncompact SO(1,3) in this finite vector representation.
Gauge redundancy could make the apparent Cartan background unobservable, but requires an explicit mechanism.
The calculation concerns the fundamental representation and fixed backgrounds.
nextBranches: Promote the Cartan involution to an auxiliary field and test whether integrating it out restores Lorentz covariance.
Explore constrained one-vector compensator models that do not require a positive alignment metric.
Quantify preferred-frame operators induced if the Cartan metric remains weakly coupled.
